changes: Read bounded ordinary String-literal class annotation arguments from comment-stripped source aligned with the string mask. Typed metadata tokens preserve header boundaries even when quoted text contains braces, angle brackets or escaped quotes.

The existing independent-return proof can now handle these class headers. Annotation values are discarded; they establish no safe value, target identity or effect fact. No annotation-name allowlist or change to the helper body, summary schema or renderer is introduced.
limits: Only leading class annotation markers, empty arguments, one default String literal or unique named String-literal values are supported. Numeric, boolean, char, null, identifier, expression, class, nested or array values remain unknown.
The ordinary escape subset is bounded; octal, Unicode preprocessing, text blocks and unsupported escapes remain unknown. Existing header/token/annotation and shared proof limits are preserved.

Caller annotations retain the marker-only grammar. Generic caller/class scope, exact private target/types, opaque references, uncertain String conversions, effect rejection, all-return proof and local-only compatibility boundaries are unchanged.

This adds header coverage rather than Java type resolution, HTML encoding or output-context knowledge. Safe formatter carriers can still remain findings when their scalar values lack the required provenance.
The inherited recognized-sink/local-constant enclosing-expression gap remains; no new helper fact enters that compatibility path.
reassessment: The measured header extension removes 22 OWASP false positives without changing recall. The inspected direct SQL helper examples are now quiet; two inspected literal-format carrier examples remain findings. Next, prove every carrier element independently under one shared budget, using only local scalar provenance and the existing pure private helper route. Apply this only to complete current printf statements with genuine context; preserve the old renderer and prior-output replay so no new HTML or later-stream claim is introduced.
